thread_b.role: lockless stall-warning reader (SUBSTITUTED for the annotated 2nd writer; see notes)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(rnp->exp_tasks)]) from thread_b (the lockless stall/boost read of the pointer must not interleave with a conflicting store)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the writers hold rnp->lock, but the stall-warning reader tests/traverses rnp->exp_tasks WITHOUT taking rnp->lock first (rcu_boost_kthread similarly); a one-sided lock does not serialize the lockless read → no g establishes atomic(read)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single pointer read; an unmarked lockless load concurrent with a conflicting store → data race

fix_maps_to: WRITE_ONCE on all exp_tasks stores + READ_ONCE/data_race on lockless loads, AND rcu_print_task_exp_stall now takes raw_spin_lock_irqsave_rcu_node(rnp) before traversing exp_tasks → adds serialize(rnp->lock, [stall traversal]) to the reader, establishing atomic over the read/traversal (the *_ONCE additions remove tearing on the already-lock-protected accesses)
recall_risk_notes: MAJOR MODELING MISMATCH: the flow_annotation's literal pair is TWO writes — rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_irqrestore:503 and sync_rcu_exp_select_node_cpus:376 — but BOTH execute under rnp->lock (confirmed: lock taken at tree_plugin.h:487, and tree_exp.h:377 releases it), so they are mutually exclusive and do NOT race with each other. Fed that exact pair, our grounding would (correctly) mark protected=true and reject → FN against the annotated pair. The true KCSAN race is a locked WRITE vs a LOCKLESS READER (rcu_print_task_exp_stall stall-warning traversal, rcu_boost_kthread), so I substituted that lockless reader as thread_b. Recall therefore hinges on (a) our design enumerating the stall/boost reader as a concurrent root (a debug/RCU-stall path it may not treat as a thread) and (b) pairing it with a writer rather than pairing the two writers. Maintainer notes the unprotected traversal only happens during an expedited RCU CPU-stall warning — very low production likelihood (benign).
